intro.p: This manual describes the scripting codes you can use when you build a New Centurions scenario: what each code does, what its Extra Codes mean, and the small details that decide whether your scripts behave the way you meant. It describes the game as the 1.3.2 release plays it.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Takes the party into the clinic screen at once, with prices scaled by a percentage you choose. An optional sound plays and an optional text is shown first.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Clinic price percentage
2) Sound (0 for none)
3) Text number (0 for none)
1) 100 gives the clinic's normal prices. Higher values make treatment dearer, lower values cheaper.
2) A sound number played as the party walks in. 0 plays nothing.
3) A text number shown before the clinic opens. The clinic screen appears when the player dismisses the text. 0 shows no text and opens the clinic straight away.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Entering the clinic gathers the credits each warrior carries into the party's purse, even if the player buys nothing. When the player leaves the clinic, the script carries on with the step after this one.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A field hospital at the end of a bridge fight. Extra Codes 40 holds 50, 2200, 310: treatment costs half price, sound 2200 plays, text 310 ("The medic waves you in") is shown, and then the clinic opens.

codes.title: Pick warriors, then invert the picks

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The number of warriors to pick. The sign of the ID decides whether fallen warriors can be picked (see Options).

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Works like Code 14, except that when the player has finished, every warrior who was picked becomes unpicked and every warrior who was not picked becomes picked.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: The sign of the ID works as in Code 14.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Use it to say "the rest of you": ask the player to pick the one warrior who stays behind to guard the gate, and the steps that follow then act on everyone else. Names in later texts follow the same rules as for Code 14.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 1. The player picks Marcus to stand watch. Marcus ends up unpicked and the other five warriors end up picked, so a following Code 15 hurts everyone but Marcus.

sections.label: Caution
paragraphs: The sign of the ID is subject to the Caution under Code 14.

codes.title: Clear objects from an area of a map

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Removes every placed object from a rectangle of cells on any map of the scenario. The terrain under the objects is left alone. Use it to take away a gate, a barrel or a campfire once the story has moved past it.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Map number
2) Left column of the rectangle
3) Right column of the rectangle
4) Top row of the rectangle
5) Bottom row of the rectangle
1) The map to change. It does not have to be the map the party is standing on.
2) and 3) Columns run from 0 to 89. The left column must not be greater than the right column, or nothing happens.
4) and 5) Rows run from 0 to 89. The top row must not be greater than the bottom row, or nothing happens.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The change is saved with the map, and the map the party is on is then reloaded and redrawn, so the player sees the objects vanish at once if they were in view. This code clears objects only. To change terrain tiles use Code 12.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A toll gate stands on map 4 at columns 20 to 21, row 33. Once the party pays, a Code -12 with E-Codes 4, 20, 21, 33, 33 removes the gate and the road is open.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A text number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Shows the text and waits for the player to dismiss it.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: The game passes a negative ID on to its text routine unchanged. What it does was not confirmed, so use a positive ID.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Names inside the text can be filled in as it is shown. ^1 to ^6 stand for the first to sixth warrior of the squad. If that warrior is down, the name of the last warrior still standing is used instead. ^9 stands for the warrior chosen by the most recent pick (Code 14, -14 or 31) and keeps that name until the next pick. Code 3 takes its question text from the step before it, so a Code 3 step normally follows a Code 1 step.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 12 shows text 12, "^1 spots a trip wire across the corridor." The first warrior's name appears in place of ^1.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Plays an optional sound, shows an optional text, then starts a battle. The script resumes after the battle.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Battle number (or the lowest of a range)
2) Highest battle number (0 for a single battle)
3) Sound (0 for none)
4) Text shown before the battle (0 for none)
5) Reward mode
1) The battle to fight.
2) If this is 0, the battle in E-Code 1 is fought. Otherwise a battle number from E-Code 1 to E-Code 2 is chosen at random, both ends included.
3) A sound number played before the fight.
4) A text number shown before the fight.
5) 0 gives the normal rewards. 5 gives victory points only. The effect of any other value was not confirmed; test it in your scenario before relying on it.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Code 100 pays the rewards itself. Once it has run in a battle's script, this code does not pay them a second time.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A bandit ambush. Extra Codes 7 holds 14, 17, 1500, 88, 0: one of battles 14 to 17 is chosen, sound 1500 plays, text 88 is shown, and the normal rewards follow a victory.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Asks the player a question and acts on the answer. The question text is the text of the step just before this one, so that step is normally a Code 1.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Which answer triggers the outcome
2) Outcome
3) Outcome number
4) Label of the left button
5) Label of the right button
1) 0 means the outcome happens when the player answers yes (and the script carries on if the answer is no). Any other value means the outcome happens on no (and the script carries on after yes).

2) What the triggering answer does: 0 moves the party back one step and ends the script, 1 replaces the script, 2 jumps into a branch of the simple encounter now running, 3 jumps into a branch of the typed encounter now running, 4 ends the script. Any other value carries on with the next step.
3) For outcome 1, the number of the script that takes over. For outcomes 2 and 3, the branch to run, 0 to 3. Not used by the other outcomes.
4) and 5) Text numbers for the two button labels. 0 gives "Yes" and "No".

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Outcome 2 or 3 uses the encounter of that kind that is on screen. Without one the game uses whatever branch data it last held, so use these outcomes only inside such an encounter.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A toll bridge. Step 1 is Code 1 with the toll keeper's demand, step 2 is Code 3 with Extra Codes 30 holding 1, 1, 12, 0, 0. If the player answers no, script 12 (the guards draw swords) replaces this one. If yes, the script carries on to the payment step.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A simple encounter number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Shows the encounter's text with up to four choices. The choice the player makes runs that choice's own short script of eight steps.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The encounter sound plays when it opens. The encounter can limit the number of visits. If the player cancels, the party steps back to where it came from. Codes 35 and 41 remove choices from a simple encounter and Code 34 leaves it.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 6 opens simple encounter 6, "The Strange Console", with the choices Touch it, Scan it, Smash it and Leave.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A typed encounter number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Opens an encounter that answers to what the player does or types, up to the maximum number of tries the encounter allows.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: When the player runs out of tries on the last visit, the encounter takes its timeout result. Cancelling steps the party back one square. Code 34 leaves the encounter and Code 44 removes one of its branches.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 3 opens typed encounter 3, a locked door that opens when the right word is typed.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A shop number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Loads the shop and, for a zero or negative ID, opens the shop window straight away.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: A zero or negative ID opens the shop window at once, using the number without its sign. A positive ID only makes that shop the current one, so the party reaches it through the shop control while it stays there.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Opening a shop this way removes any limit set by Code 111, whatever the sign of the ID, even when no window opens. The script resumes when the player leaves the shop.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID -4 opens shop 4, a quartermaster's tent, as soon as the step runs.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Overwrites the eight steps of a map event, or of one branch of an encounter, with the steps of another script.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Map number (-1 for a simple encounter, -2 for a typed encounter)
2) Event number or encounter number
3) Script holding the new steps
4) Not used
5) Branch of the encounter to replace (encounters only)
1) The map holding the event. -1 and -2 replace a branch of an encounter instead.
2) For a map, an event number from 0 to 99. For -1 and -2, the encounter number.
3) The script whose eight steps become the event's new steps.
5) For encounters, the branch to replace, 0 to 3. Stay inside this range.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The change is kept for the rest of the game. For a map event, its chance of running is not changed.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: After the player cuts the rope bridge, Extra Codes 52 holds 3, 14, 90, 0, 0: event 14 on map 3 now runs script 90, "the bridge is gone", instead of its old script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An event number on the current map.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Copies the eight steps of that event over the running script and starts again from the first step.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The steps are copied from the event as it stands now, including any change made by Code 7. The ID must not be negative. The chance of the event is not copied. Before the script starts again, the game tests the chance of the running event once more: if it is below 1 the script ends, and otherwise a roll of 1 to 100 above the chance ends the script without a word. Give an event that uses Code 8 a chance of 100.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Three fountains all use the same event. Each fountain's own event has a chance of 100 and holds one Code 8 step with ID 20, so changing event 20 changes all of them. Event 20 ends with Code 24 so that the fountains can be used again.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A sound number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Plays the sound and goes on to the next step.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: The game passes a negative ID on to its sound routine unchanged. What it does was not confirmed, so use a positive ID.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 4100 plays a door slamming just before a battle step.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A treasure number from the scenario's treasure list.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Opens the treasure window for that treasure so the party can take it.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The script resumes when the player closes the window.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 22 opens treasure 22, the cache behind the false wall.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The number of victory points.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Shares the victory points among the party and opens the treasure window that shows them.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 150 awards 150 victory points for solving the vault puzzle.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Replaces one tile on a map, either the floor tile or the object on it.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Map number
2) Column (x)
3) Row (y)
4) New tile number
5) Layer
1) The map to change. It does not have to be the current map.
2) and 3) The tile position, 0 to 89 for each.
4) The tile that goes in. On the object layer, a number of 23000 or more has 23000 taken off before it is stored.
5) 2 changes the object layer. Any other value changes the floor layer.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Use this to open a gate, collapse a corridor or remove a barrel. Code -12 clears objects from a whole rectangle at once.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 61 holds 2, 40, 17, 305, 2: on map 2, the object at column 40, row 17 becomes tile 305 (an open gate).

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes the chance that map events run when the party steps on them, for one event, for a range of events, or both.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Map number
2) One event number (0 for none)
3) New chance
4) First event of a range (0 for none)
5) Last event of the range
1) The map holding the events.
2) A single event to change, 0 to 99.
3) The new chance. A negative value switches the event off, which is how the game itself marks a spent event.
4) and 5) A range of events, both ends included. E-Code 4 must be 0 or at most E-Code 5, and both must be within 0 to 99.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 18 holds 5, 12, 100, 20, 24: on map 5, event 12 gets a 100 chance and events 20 to 24 get the same.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The number of warriors to pick. The sign of the ID decides whether fallen warriors can be picked (see Options).

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Clears every earlier pick and asks the player to choose that many warriors. The steps that follow can act on the picked warriors only.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: With a positive ID, only warriors who are up can be picked, and the count is lowered if fewer are available. With a negative ID, the count is its value without the sign and everyone can be picked.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Picks are cleared even if the player picks nobody. Codes 15, 17, 30 and others read the picks. Code -14 inverts the picks when the player finishes.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 2: "Choose two warriors to cross the ice." The next step is a Code 15 that hurts the picked pair.

sections.label: Caution
paragraphs: Which sign lets fallen warriors be picked, and how the count is lowered when fewer warriors are available, was not confirmed down to the last detail. Test both signs in your scenario before relying on them.

codes.title: Heal or hurt the picked warriors

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes the stamina of each picked warrior by a random amount, then shows an optional text.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Multiplier
2) Lowest random number
3) Highest random number
4) Sound (0 for none)
5) Text (0 for none)
1) The random number is multiplied by this. A negative multiplier hurts.
2) and 3) A number from E-Code 2 to E-Code 3 is drawn separately for each picked warrior.
4) A sound played for each warrior affected.
5) A text shown once, after all warriors have been changed.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A warrior brought to zero stamina or below is down, and if this takes the whole squad the mission is lost.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 9 holds -1, 3, 8, 3000, 70: each picked warrior loses 3 to 8 stamina, sound 3000 plays for each, then text 70 appears.

codes.title: Heal or hurt the whole party

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: The same as Code 15, but every warrior is affected, not only the picked ones.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: The same five as Code 15.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A separate random number is drawn for each warrior.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 10 holds 1, 5, 5, 0, 71: every warrior regains 5 stamina and text 71 follows.

codes.title: Cast a scan on the picked warriors

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Casts a scan on each picked warrior as though from a scripted source, using the scan's normal effects.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Scan number
2) Power level
3) Saving throw adjustment
4) Force the effect
1) The scan to cast.
2) The power level of the scan.
3) Added to each target's saving throw. Negative values make it harder to resist.
4) Any nonzero value forces the effect: the scan cannot be resisted.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: If the casting brings every warrior down, the mission is lost. Test the power level and force settings in your scenario before relying on them for a balanced effect.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 15 holds 33, 2, 0, 0: scan 33 hits each picked warrior at power 2 with their normal saving throw.

codes.title: Cast a scan on the whole party

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: The same as Code 17, but the whole squad is picked first and then affected.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: The same four as Code 17.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The earlier picks are replaced by the whole squad.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 16 holds 33, 1, 0, 1: scan 33 strikes every warrior and cannot be resisted.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Picks a text number at random from a range and shows it.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Lowest text number
2) Highest text number
1) and 2) A text from E-Code 1 to E-Code 2 is chosen at random, both ends included, and shown.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 4 holds 200, 205: one of six rumours, texts 200 to 205, is shown.

codes.title: Move the party and start the event there

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Moves the party to another place, possibly on another map, plays an optional sound and text, then starts any event on the square where it arrives.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Map number
2) Column (x)
3) Row (y)
4) Sound (0 for none)
5) Text (0 for none)
1) A negative value stays on the current map.
2) and 3) The destination square, 0 to 89. A negative value keeps the current column or row.
4) A sound played on arrival.
5) A text shown on arrival.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: If the arrival square holds an event, that event takes over the running script after the text is dismissed, so the steps after Code 20 never run. The event first passes its own chance test. Place the party on a square with no event to just move it.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 25 holds 6, 10, 80, 2400, 0: the party appears on map 6 at column 10, row 80, and sound 2400 plays.

codes.title: Branch if the party has an item

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Looks for an item anywhere in the party's packs, takes one path if it is found, and another if it is not.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Item number
2) Where to go if the item is found
3) What to do if it is not found
4) Target if the item is found
5) Script to run if it is not found
1) The item to look for.
2) 0 replaces the script with script E-Code 4, 1 opens simple encounter E-Code 4, 2 opens typed encounter E-Code 4. Any other value carries on.
3) 0 replaces the script with script E-Code 5. 3 ends the script. Any other value carries on.
4) The script or encounter number for E-Code 2.
5) The script number used when E-Code 3 is 0.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The item is not taken. Code 22 removes it.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A locked vault. Extra Codes 40 holds 77, 0, 0, 50, 51: if someone carries item 77 (the brass key), script 50 (the door opens) runs, otherwise script 51 (the door stays shut).

codes.title: Change items held by the party

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Removes an item, changes its charges, or swaps it for another item.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Item number
2) How many to affect
3) Action
4) Charges to add
5) Replacement item
1) The item to look for in the packs.
2) The most copies affected.
3) 1 removes the item. 2 adds charges. 3 replaces the item with the item in E-Code 5.
4) For action 2, the charges added. A negative number drains charges. An item left with no charges that is meant to be discarded when empty is removed.
5) For action 3, the item that replaces it.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Worn items are taken off properly when they are removed or replaced. Test the empty-item behaviour in your scenario before relying on it.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 33 holds 77, 1, 1, 0, 0: one copy of item 77 (the brass key) is removed from whoever carries it.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes how often random battles occur in one region of a map, and which battles they can be.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Map number
2) Region number
3) New encounter chance
4) New lowest battle number
5) New highest battle number
1) The map holding the region. It does not have to be the current map.
2) The region, 0 to 19.
3) The new chance of a random battle. It always replaces the old value.
4) and 5) The new lowest and highest battle numbers. A negative value leaves that limit as it was.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Set E-Code 3 to 0 to make a region quiet. Test the chance scale in your scenario before relying on exact odds.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 12 holds 1, 4, 0, -1, -1: region 4 on map 1 has no more random battles.

codes.title: End the script and keep the event

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Ends the script. The map event that started it is kept, so it can run again.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A script started by a map event that runs out of steps, with no encounter on screen, leaves the event spent: its chance becomes -1 and it does not run again. Use Code 24 for events the party may visit more than once. "Moving Between Scripts" lists the steps that leave a script at once without marking the event. Code 24 also clears an encounter that is on screen.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A merchant's stall event ends with Code 24 so the party can come back.

codes.title: Remember the party's position for the event

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Notes the square the party is on so that, when the script finishes, the event is stored with that position.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The script does not end here; the steps after it still run. Inside an encounter's choice it also stops the encounter from being shown again when the script ends. Test this code in your scenario before relying on it.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A trap event uses Code 25 before a teleport step.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Shows a small "Click Mouse" box with a sound and waits for the player to click.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Use it to pace a sequence of pictures or sounds.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Between two Code 27 steps that show pictures, a Code 26 lets the player look at the first.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A picture number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Draws the picture, centred in the 320 by 320 look area, replacing what was there.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The picture must exist in the scenario or in the game's shared data. The game does not handle a missing picture, so check every picture number.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID 600 shows picture 600, a portrait of the warlord.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Redraws the main view.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Use it after a picture to return to the map.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: After Code 27 and Code 26, a Code 28 brings back the map.

codes.title: Give or show a map note

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A note number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Gives the party the note, and either announces it or shows it right away.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: With a positive ID, a short "gained" message flashes and the note can be viewed later from the notes menu. With a negative ID, the note is shown at once and the script waits until the player closes it.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The note number is the ID without its sign.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: ID -3 gives the party the old map, note 3, and shows it immediately.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Narrows the picked warriors to those who pass a test of a special skill or an attribute.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Special skill number or attribute number
2) Kind of test
3) Who is tested
4) Invert the result
5) Attribute threshold
1) For a special skill test, the skill number. For an attribute test, 0 to 6: Brawn, Knowledge, Judgement, Quickness, Coordination, Vitality, Psionics.
2) 0 tests a special skill. Any other value tests the attribute.
3) 1 tests the whole squad. 2 tests every warrior with stamina above 0. Any other value tests only those already picked.
4) Any nonzero value picks the warriors who failed and drops those who passed. Warriors who were not tested are picked too, because every warrior's pick is turned round.
5) An attribute test passes when the attribute is above this number.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A special skill test rolls 1 to 100 and passes when the roll is not above the skill plus its bonus. The skill value is read from the warrior whose place in the squad matches this step's place in the script, which is not always the warrior under test; test this in your scenario before relying on it. An attribute test uses no dice.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 8 holds 0, 1, 1, 0, 14: everyone is tested, and those with Brawn above 14 are picked.

codes.title: Ask the player to pick a warrior and test them

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Asks the player to pick one living warrior, tests that warrior, and runs a different script for a pass and a fail.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Special skill number or attribute number
2) Threshold
3) Kind of test
4) Script on a pass
5) Script on a fail
1) For an attribute, 0 to 5: Brawn, Knowledge, Judgement, Quickness, Vitality, Psionics. Any other attribute number makes the script carry on without a test.
2) A special skill passes when the skill plus its bonus reaches this number. An attribute passes when it is above this number.
3) 0 tests a special skill. Any other value tests the attribute.
4) and 5) The script that replaces this one.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: There are no dice. The warrior chosen is the one named by ^9 in later texts.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 5 holds 0, 12, 0, 60, 61: the player picks the one who tries to pick the lock; if their lockpicking skill and bonus reach 12, script 60 runs, otherwise script 61.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Tries to take credits from the party. Depending on whether it can, the script goes on or jumps.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Cost in credits
2) Condition
3) Jump type
4) Jump target
5) Step to start at in the target
1) The amount to take. It comes from the party's purse first, then from the credits warriors carry. If the party cannot pay, nothing is taken and the game warns that the party cannot pay.

2) 0 jumps if the party could not pay. 1 jumps if it did pay. 2 always jumps. -1 goes straight to the eighth step of this script if the party could not pay (the script otherwise goes on). Other values never jump.

3) The standard jump: -1 runs the eighth step of this script next. 0 replaces the script with script E-Code 4. 1 runs a branch of the simple encounter now running, and 2 a branch of the typed encounter now running, with E-Code 4 as the branch number (0 to 3). 3 ends the script, keeps the event and clears the encounter, like Code 24. Other values do not jump.
4) The script number, or the branch number for jump types 1 and 2.
5) For jump types 1 and 2, the step to start from, counted from 0: 0 is the first step and 7 the eighth.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The standard jump is used in the same way by Codes 38 and 42.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A toll bridge. Extra Codes 71 holds 25, 0, 0, 90, 0: if the party cannot pay 25 credits, script 90 (the guards bar the way) replaces this one.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Leaves the simple or typed encounter now running and carries on with the step after the one that opened it.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Use it only in a script that runs from an encounter opened with Code 4 or Code 5. It puts back the copy of the script saved when the encounter opened (see "Moving Between Scripts"); with no encounter open there is no copy to trust, so do not use it elsewhere.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A "Walk away" choice in a simple encounter runs a script whose only step is Code 34.

codes.title: Remove a choice from the running simple encounter

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The choice to remove, 1 to 4.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Blanks that choice in the simple encounter now running and shows the encounter again.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The change is kept. It only works inside a simple encounter.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: After the player takes the idol, a Code 35 with ID 2 removes the "Take the idol" choice.

codes.title: Take or return the party's belongings

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: Nonzero to take, 0 to return.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Takes all the party's items and credits and stores them, or gives them back.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: A nonzero ID does nothing if goods are already stored. 0 does nothing if nothing is stored.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Taking shows a message and drops every item the warriors have, including worn ones. Returning puts the items back and re-wears what was worn, then opens the treasure window if at least one item came back. Returned credits alone open no window.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Prisoners being searched: Code 36 with ID 1 at the cell door, and Code 36 with ID 0 once the party escapes.

codes.title: Branch if the party has an item (standard jump)

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Checks whether the party carries an item and jumps accordingly.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Item number
2) Condition
3) Jump type
4) Jump target
5) Step to start at in the target
1) The item to look for.
2) 0 jumps if the item is not carried. 1 jumps if it is. 2 always jumps. Other values never jump.
3) to 5) The standard jump described in Code 33.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 44 holds 90, 0, 0, 12, 0: if nobody has item 90 (the pass), script 12 replaces this one.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: A script number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Replaces the running script with that script and starts it from its first step.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Use it to continue a long scene beyond eight steps.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The eighth step of script 5 is Code 39 with ID 6, which carries the scene on.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Checks one of the party's lasting conditions, the timed effects that apply to the whole squad, and jumps if it is set or clear.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Jump when set or clear
2) Jump type
3) Target
4) Condition number
1) 1 jumps if the condition is present. 2 jumps if it is absent. Other values never jump.
2) 1 replaces the script with script E-Code 3. 2 opens simple encounter E-Code 3. 3 opens typed encounter E-Code 3. Any other value ends the script.
3) The script or encounter number.
4) The index of the party condition to test, counted from 0. Index 0 is the party's light.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 6 holds 2, 1, 40, 0: if condition 0 (the party's light) is absent, script 40 runs.

codes.title: Remove a choice from any simple encounter

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Blanks a choice of a stored simple encounter, which need not be the one running.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Simple encounter number
2) Choice number
1) The encounter to change.
2) The choice to blank, 1 to 4. Use only these values.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The change is kept for the rest of the game.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 7 holds 12, 3: choice 3 of encounter 12 can no longer be picked.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Rolls a chance. If it succeeds, the script ends or jumps. If not, it carries on.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Chance percent
2) What a success does
3) Jump type
4) Jump target
5) Step to start at in the target
1) The roll is 1 to 100 and succeeds when it is not above this number. 100 always succeeds and 0 never does.

2) -2 ends the script, and the event is spent as when the steps run out. 1 uses the standard jump from E-Codes 3 to 5. 2 ends the script and keeps the event, but unlike Code 24 it does not clear an encounter that is on screen. Other values carry on.
3) to 5) The standard jump described in Code 33.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Extra Codes 20 holds 30, 1, 0, 70, 0: with a 30 percent chance, script 70 replaces this one.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Puts a condition (poison, blindness, and so on) on some of your warriors for a set time, or for good.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Who is affected.
2) Condition number.
3) Duration.
4) Sound number.
1) 0 affects the whole squad. 1 affects only the picked warriors. 2 affects every warrior who is still alive (stamina above -10).
2) The number of the condition in the game's condition list, for example 3 for Poisoned, 27 for Blind, 28 for Diseased or 29 for Confused.
3) The number is added to the warrior's current value for that condition. A positive number is a timed condition. A negative number stays until something removes it.
4) The sound is played once for each warrior who receives the condition. Use 0 for no sound.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Before it gives anything, this code clears every running timed value of the chosen condition on every warrior in the squad, including warriors it does not select. A permanent (negative) condition is not cleared by this step, but the duration in E-Code 3 is then added to it for every warrior it selects: a permanent -1 with a duration of 6 becomes a timed 5, and a negative duration makes a permanent condition longer. Each affected warrior then shows the spell effect and the condition result.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A cursed idol blinds whoever lifts it. Use E1 = 1 after picking the warrior who touched it, E2 = 27, E3 = 6, E4 = a hissing sound. Every warrior's old blindness timer is cleared first, then only the picked warrior is blinded for 6.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The number of the choice to remove, 1 to 4.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Empties one choice of the typed encounter that is on screen, so that picking it afterwards closes the encounter.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The first seven steps of the choice are cleared and its eighth step becomes Code 24, so picking the choice closes the encounter and keeps the event. Use this in a script that runs from inside a typed encounter, for example after the player has opened a chest, so the same choice cannot be repeated. The game does not check the number, so stay inside 1 to 4.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: In a typed encounter at a well, choice 2 is "Draw water". The script behind choice 2 gives the squad a drink and then uses code 44 with ID 2. If the player picks choice 2 again, the encounter closes.

sections.label: Caution
paragraphs: Whether the emptied choice is still listed in the encounter was not confirmed. Test this in your scenario before relying on it.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Moves the squad to another place, on this map or another one, without running the event at the arrival square.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Map number.
2) X position.
3) Y position.
4) Sound number.
5) Text number.
1) The map to move to. -1 stays on the current map.
2) The column to arrive at. -1 keeps the current column.
3) The row to arrive at. -1 keeps the current row.
4) A sound played on arrival. 0 for none.
5) A text shown on arrival. 0 for none.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Code 20 is the version that also runs the event at the arrival square. Code 45 does not. The sound and the text happen after the squad has arrived, and the script then continues with its next action.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A rope bridge drops the squad to the cave floor. Use E1 = -1, E2 = 12, E3 = 40, E4 = a crash sound, E5 = the text "You land hard in the dark."

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Looks at a mission flag and, if the test matches, leaves the script for another place.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Mission flag number.
2) When to branch.
3) Branch type.
4) Branch number.
5) Start action.
1) The flag to look at.
2) 0 branches when the flag is clear. 1 branches when the flag is set. 2 always branches. Any other value never branches, and the script goes on to the next action.

3) -1 runs the eighth action of this script next. 0 goes to script E4 (starting at its first action). 1 runs the actions of choice E4 of the simple encounter on screen, starting at action E5. 2 does the same for the typed encounter on screen. 3 ends the script, keeps the event and clears the encounter, like code 24. Any other value does nothing.
4) For types 1 and 2, the choice number counted from 0 (0 to 3). For type 0, the script number.
5) For types 1 and 2, the action to start at, counted from 0: 0 is the first action and 7 the eighth.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The tail of this code, E3 to E5, is shared by codes 58 and 59 below. Types 1 and 2 only make sense in a script that was started from an encounter.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The guard lets you pass only if mission flag 17 (the signed pass) is set. Use E1 = 17, E2 = 1, E3 = 0, E4 = the number of the "gate opens" script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The flag number. A positive number sets the flag. Zero or a negative number clears the flag whose number is the ID without its sign.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Sets a mission flag to 1 or clears it to 0.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: An ID of 0 clears flag 0.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Mission flags are one byte each. Code 76 uses the same flags as counters, so setting a flag here overwrites any count kept there. To set a flag that is later cleared, use a positive ID in one step and the same number with a minus sign in another.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: After the dragon dies, ID 30 sets flag 30. When the queen takes back her ring, ID -30 clears it.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Runs a battle with only the picked warriors fighting, and gives the rewards when it is over.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Battle number.
2) Highest battle number.
3) Sound number.
4) Text number.
5) Treasure number.
1) The battle to fight. Battle numbers work as in code 2.
2) 0 fights battle E1. Any other number picks a random battle from E1 up to E2, both included.
3) A sound played before the fight. 0 for none.
4) A text shown before the fight. 0 for none.
5) A treasure given after a victory, in addition to the normal booty. 0 for none.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Afterwards every warrior of the squad is counted as present again. If no warrior is left standing, the game shows a short message and gives out a reduced set of rewards that was not confirmed; test this in your scenario. Otherwise the normal booty comes first, then the treasure in E5. The map is reloaded afterwards.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Three scouts surprise the squad at a ford. Pick the two fastest warriors, then use E1 = 14, E2 = 0, E3 = a horn call, E4 = the ambush text, E5 = 6.

codes.title: Pick by Race, Gender, M.O.S. or Class

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Picks the warriors who match a trait. Later codes (55, 60, 74 and others) act on them.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) What to test.
2) Gender.
3) Race, M.O.S. or class number.
5) Living only.
1) 0 tests the race. 1 tests the gender. 2 tests the M.O.S. 3 tests the race class. 4 tests the M.O.S. class.
2) The gender number to pick. It is read only when E1 is 1.
3) The race number (E1 = 0), the M.O.S. number (E1 = 2), or the class number (E1 = 3 or 4).
5) 0 considers every warrior. Any other value considers only warriors with stamina above 0.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Everyone is unpicked first, so this code replaces the old group. E4 is not read. Test the gender numbers in your scenario before relying on them.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Only dwarves can read the runes. Use E1 = 0, E3 = the dwarf's race number, E5 = 1.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes a shop's prices and the stock of one item in it.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Shop number.
2) Price change.
3) Item number.
4) Stock change.
1) The shop to change.
2) Added to the shop's price percentage. Use a negative number for a discount.
3) The item whose stock is changed. Every slot of the shop holding this item is changed.

4) Added to the number in stock. Only the low byte is used, and the stock is one signed byte: a result below 0 becomes 0, and a result past 127 wraps round to a negative number and so also becomes 0. Keep E4 small.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The change is saved, so it is still there the next time the squad visits.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: After the squad frees the merchant's caravan, use E1 = 4, E2 = -15, E3 = the number of healing salve, E4 = 5.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Picks warriors by a test on each of them.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) The test.
2) The test value.
3) Which warriors are tested.

1) 0 picks warriors whose movement is below E2. 1 picks warriors whose place in the squad (counted from 1) is below E2. 2 picks warriors who carry item E2. 3 picks each warrior with a chance of E2 percent. 4 picks warriors who fail a saving throw against attribute E2 (0 to 5). 5 picks warriors who fail a saving throw against resistance type E2 (0 to 8). 6 picks the warrior currently selected on screen. 7 picks warriors who are wearing item E2.
3) 0 tests every warrior. 1 tests only warriors with stamina above 0. 2 is meant to test only the already picked warriors.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Everyone is unpicked first, so mode 2 never finds anybody. Test 3 draws one random number for each warrior tested. Tests 4 and 5 draw their own numbers too. A test number above 7 picks nobody.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The ghoul's touch paralyzes the unwary. Use E1 = 4, E2 = 3 (the fourth attribute), E3 = 1. Every living warrior who fails the save is picked.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Picks warriors by their M.O.S., either one M.O.S. or a whole group of them.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) M.O.S. number.
2) Group.
3) Which warriors are tested.
1) A single M.O.S. to pick.
2) 0 for no group. 1 also picks M.O.S. 1, 3 and 4. 2 also picks M.O.S. 3, 6, 7 and 8. 3 also picks M.O.S. 2 and 5.
3) 0 tests every warrior. 1 tests only warriors with stamina above 0. 2 is meant to test only picked warriors.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Everyone is unpicked first, so mode 2 never picks anybody. E1 and E2 add together: a warrior is picked if either matches. If you only want the group, give E1 a number that no warrior has.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A priest is needed to open the vault. Use E1 = the priest's M.O.S. number, E2 = 0, E3 = 1.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes one entry of the scenario's calendar: how likely it is to run, how often, and the day it comes due.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Calendar entry number.
2) Chance in percent.
3) Interval in days.
4) Reset to today.
5) Days to add.
1) The entry to change.
2) The new chance. A negative number leaves the chance as it is.
3) The new interval. A negative number leaves the interval as it is.
4) Any value except 0 sets the entry's due day to the current game day.
5) Days added to the due day, after step 4 has been applied. A negative number adds nothing.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: An entry number past the end of the calendar is not allowed.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A wandering merchant's visit should be postponed a week after the squad robs him. Use E1 = 3, E2 = -1, E3 = -1, E4 = 1, E5 = 7.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Checks how many warriors are picked and sends the script to one of two places.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) What to check.
2) If the check fails.
4) Script if the check passes.
5) Script if the check fails.

1) 0 passes when at least one warrior is picked. 1 to 6 pass when the first warrior is picked. Any other number, including a negative one, passes when exactly that many warriors (without the sign) are picked.
2) 1 goes to script E5. Any other value ends the script.
4) The script to start when the check passes.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Values 1 to 6 all look only at the first warrior, not at the warrior of that number. E3 is not read.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The ferryman takes exactly two passengers. After picking two warriors, use E1 = 2, E2 = 1, E4 = the boarding script, E5 = the "too many or too few" script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Fights a battle in which the squad may retreat, and tells the game where to go if it does.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Battle number.
2) Highest battle number.
3) Retreat script.
4) Sound number.
5) Text number.
1) The battle to fight, as in code 2.
2) 0 fights battle E1. Any other number picks a random battle from E1 to E2.
3) -1 steps the squad back to where it stood before. Any other number is a script that runs when the squad retreats.
4) A sound played before the fight. 0 for none.
5) A text shown before the fight. 0 for none.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: If the squad wins, the normal booty is given and the script goes on. If it retreats and E3 is -1, the game warns the player, plays a sound, adds 200 times the warrior's level to each warrior's remaining victory points, and steps the squad back. Test this penalty in your scenario before relying on it. If it retreats and E3 is another number, that script starts.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The squad fights its way into the arena. Use E1 = 9, E2 = 0, E3 = -1, E4 = 0, E5 = 0. If the squad runs, it is back at the gate and each warrior needs more victory points before the next level.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes the tile set used by a map, and whether the map is dark.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Look number.
2) Dark.
3) Map number.
1) The new tile set. Only the low byte is used.
2) The new darkness value. Only the low byte is used.
3) The map to change.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The change is saved with the map. The map the squad is on stays the current map afterwards.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: After the volcano erupts, use E1 = the ash-covered tile set, E2 = 1, E3 = the village map.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Does something only if the game is played at a given difficulty level or harder.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Difficulty level.
2) What to do when it passes.
3) Branch type (as in code 46).
4) Branch number.
5) Start action.
1) The test passes when this number is no greater than the current difficulty level.
2) 1 uses the branch given by E3 to E5. 2 ends the script and keeps its codes. -2 ends the script. Any other value does nothing.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: E3 to E5 work as in code 46.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: An extra troll guards the bridge only on harder settings. Use E1 = 3, E2 = 1, E3 = 0, E4 = the troll script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Looks at the tile the squad stands on.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Tile number.
2) What to do.
3) Branch type (as in code 46).
4) Branch number.
5) Start action.
1) The tile number. It is not used: the test always passes.
2) 1 uses the branch given by E3 to E5. 2 ends the script and keeps its codes. -2 ends the script. Any other value does nothing.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Because the test always passes, this code behaves as an unconditional jump or end. Do not rely on E1 to tell tiles apart.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A script that must end in a hurry can use E2 = -2.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Takes all the credits a warrior carries, for example when thieves strike.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: 2) Who loses credits.
2) 0 takes the credits of every warrior. Any other value takes them only from the picked warriors.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The credits are gone, not given to anyone. E1 is not used.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A pickpocket works the crowd. Pick the warrior he robs and use E2 = 1.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Nudges the squad's position on the map by a few squares, steady or random.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
2) Squares across (X).
3) Squares down (Y).
4) Random.
2) The number of squares to move across. A negative number moves the other way.
3) The number of squares to move down. A negative number moves the other way.

4) 0 moves exactly by E2 and E3. Any other value moves by a random amount: for each direction there is a fifty-fifty chance of each sign, and a random distance from 1 up to E2 across and from 1 up to E3 down. Use positive numbers there.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: E1 is not used. The map view is re-centred afterwards. No event runs at the new square.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A teleport trap misfires. Use E2 = 4, E3 = 4, E4 = 1.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The number of the text to show.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Plays a text in the scrolling-text window.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The view is re-centred after the text. How the lines scroll and how long the text stays up are the game's own; check a long text in your scenario before relying on its pacing.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A prophecy is read from a scroll. Use the text number of the prophecy.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Sets the game clock, or moves it forward.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Mode.
2) Days.
3) Hours.
4) Minutes.
1) 1 sets the clock to the given day, hour and minute. 2 adds the given amounts. Any other value changes nothing.

2) The day.
3) The hour, 0 to 23.
4) The minute, 0 to 59.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: There is no "keep" value: a -1 in set mode is stored as -1. In add mode, an hour that passes 23 moves to the next day, and a minute that passes 59 moves to the next hour. The minutes are checked after the hours, so many minutes can leave the hour at 24. After the change the game runs one time update in which no time passes. If the hour reads 24, the day rolls over and calendar entries (code 54) that come due may run; check this in your scenario if you set hour 24.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The squad sleeps in the inn. Use E1 = 2, E2 = 0, E3 = 8, E4 = 0 to move the clock forward eight hours.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Goes to one script if it is early enough, another if it is late.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Day.
2) Hour.
3) Hour (second test).
4) Script if on time.
5) Script if late.
1) The last day that counts as on time.
2) The last hour that counts as on time.
3) A second hour limit, compared with the current hour the same way as E2.
4) The script to start when on time.
5) The script to start when late.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The squad is late if the current day is past E1, or the current hour is past E2, or the current hour is past E3. The hour is tested whatever the day is. A -1 does not mean "ignore"; it makes the test late. Set E3 to 23 if you do not want it to matter. Both targets must be real script numbers.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The bridge keeper only sees travelers on day 5 or earlier, up to hour 18. Use E1 = 5, E2 = 18, E3 = 23, E4 = the open-bridge script, E5 = the closed-bridge script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Gives the squad random items from a range of item numbers.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Number of items.
2) Lowest item number.
3) Highest item number.
1) A positive number gives that many items. A negative number gives a random number from 1 up to the number without its sign. Use 20 or fewer.
2) Lowest item number.
3) Highest item number. Each item is chosen at random between E2 and E3, both included.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The items appear on the booty screen for the squad to take.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A treasure chest holds one to three potions. Use E1 = -3, E2 = 200, E3 = 210.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: 0 allows camping. Any other number forbids it.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Controls whether the squad may camp.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A short message appears when the setting changes. Its wording is the game's own; read both messages in your scenario. The game compares the ID itself with the old setting, which is 0 or 1, so only the IDs 0 and 1 avoid a repeated message when the code runs again; use only those two.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: In the haunted mine, ID 1 forbids camping. When the squad leaves, ID 0 allows it again.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Adds up the charges of one item over the whole squad and goes to one of two places depending on whether there are enough.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Item number.
2) Target type.
3) Charges needed.
4) Target if enough.
5) Target if not enough.
1) The item whose charges are counted. Every copy carried by every warrior is counted.

2) 0 starts script E4 or E5. 1 opens simple encounter E4 or E5. 2 opens typed encounter E4 or E5. Any other value does nothing, and the script goes on to the next action. These target types are used by every branch code below that asks for a target type.
3) The squad has enough when the total number of charges is E3 or more.
4) The target used when the squad has enough charges.
5) The target used when it does not.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: There is no "continue the script" value: whatever number you give is used as the target.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The lighthouse lamp needs 10 charges of oil. Use E1 = the oil flask, E2 = 0, E3 = 10, E4 = the "lamp burns" script, E5 = the "lamp sputters out" script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes the squad's fatigue in one step.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Mode.
3) Percent.

1) 1 sets the fatigue to 135, the top of the fatigue scale. 2 sets it to 4, the bottom of the scale. 3 multiplies the current fatigue by the result of E3 divided by 100. Any other value changes nothing.
3) Used only in mode 3. E2, E4 and E5 are not read.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: In mode 3 the division comes first and uses whole numbers, and the fatigue is then multiplied by that result. A value from 100 to 199 leaves the fatigue as it is, 200 to 299 doubles it, and below 100 makes it 0. Outside a battle, with the main window in front, the result is held between 4 and 135 at once, so 0 becomes 4. In a battle, or when the main window is not in front, the stored value stays as it is until the game's next normal update. The fatigue bar is redrawn only when the main window is in front. This manual does not say which end of the scale means rested: look at the fatigue bar in your scenario and test modes 1 and 2 before relying on them.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A mountain spring should leave the squad at the end of the scale you have found to mean rested. Use E1 = 1 or E1 = 2 accordingly.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Switches on or off three limits on Psi: the squad cannot use Psi, monsters cannot use scans, and Psi points do not recover.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) The squad cannot use Psi.
2) Monsters cannot use scans.
3) Psi points do not recover.
1) to 3) 0 lifts the limit and 1 puts it in force. The effect of other values was not confirmed; use only 0 and 1.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The limits stay as set until another code 69 changes them. The Extra Codes are read even when the ID is 0; test that case in your scenario before relying on it.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A null-field cavern blocks all Psi. On entering use E1 = 1, E2 = 1, E3 = 1; at the exit use 0, 0, 0.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Remembers where the squad stands, and later puts it back there.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: 1) Save or restore.
1) 1 saves the map, column and row of the squad. 2 restores them. Any other value does nothing.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Restoring moves the squad to the saved map and square but does not run the event there. Only one position is kept. Always save before you restore.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A trapdoor drops the squad into a pit. A script above the trapdoor saves the position with E1 = 1. When the squad climbs out, E1 = 2 puts it back.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: 0 shows the X and Y coordinates. 1 hides them.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Switches the position readout on or off.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The fatigue strip and coordinates are redrawn at once. Values other than 0 and 1 are not documented; test them in your scenario before relying on them.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: In a maze, ID 1 hides where the squad is, and ID 0 shows it again at the exit.

codes.title: Branch on Range of Mission Flags

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Goes to another place only if every mission flag in a range is set.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) First flag.
2) Last flag.
4) Target type.
5) Target.
1) The lowest flag number tested.
2) The highest flag number tested. Both ends are included.
4) The target type, as in code 67. Any other value does nothing.
5) The target number.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A flag counts as set when it is not 0. If any flag in the range is clear, the script goes on to the next action. E3 is not read.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Five seals (flags 40 to 44) guard the inner gate. Use E1 = 40, E2 = 44, E4 = 0, E5 = the gate-opens script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The number of ticks to wait.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Pauses the script before its next action.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: An ID of 0 is meant to wait as long as the player's animation-delay setting; test this in your scenario.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The pause is meant to be the ID plus one tick; this was not confirmed. This manual does not give the length of a tick; time a pause on screen in your scenario before using it for dramatic timing.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Between two lines of a speech, use ID 30 and check on screen how long the pause feels.

codes.title: Give or Take Psi Points of Picked Warriors

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Adds Psi points to, or removes them from, each picked warrior.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Rolls and direction.
2) Lowest roll.
3) Highest roll.
4) Play a sound.
5) Text number.
1) A positive number adds, a negative number takes. The size says how many rolls are made.
2) The lowest value a roll can give.
3) The highest value a roll can give. Each roll is a random number from E2 to E3, both included.
4) Any value except 0 plays a sound. The sound played is the one whose number is E2.
5) A text shown after the change. 0 for none.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Only warriors with a maximum of Psi above 0 are changed. Only the last roll for each warrior is used, not the sum, so use E1 = 1 or E1 = -1; a larger size only draws extra random numbers. Do not use 0. A warrior's Psi is held between 0 and their maximum.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A cursed shrine drains the picked warriors by 5 to 10. Use E1 = -1, E2 = 5, E3 = 10, E4 = 0, E5 = the "you feel drained" text.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Goes to another place if at least one warrior has enough Psi points.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Who is tested.
2) Psi points needed.
3) If nobody has enough.
4) Target type.
5) Target.
1) 1 tests the picked warriors. 2 tests every warrior with stamina above 0 who is not under computer control. Any other value tests nobody.
2) A warrior has enough when Psi points are this number or more.
3) 1 ends the script and keeps its codes. Any other value goes on to the next action.
4) The target type, as in code 67, used when someone has enough. Any other value does nothing.
5) The target number.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The beacon needs a warrior with 20 Psi points. Use E1 = 2, E2 = 20, E3 = 0, E4 = 0, E5 = the beacon-lit script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Adds to or subtracts from a mission flag used as a counter, and may branch when the counter is high enough.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Flag number.
2) Amount to add.
3) Branch type.
4) Threshold.
5) Target.
1) The flag to change. A flag number of 100 or more is not changed; use flags 0 to 99.
2) Added to the flag. Use a negative number to subtract.
3) 1 goes to script E5. 2 opens simple encounter E5. 3 opens typed encounter E5. Any other value does nothing.
4) 0 means never branch. Otherwise the branch happens when the flag, after the change, is E4 or more.
5) The target number.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Flags hold signed numbers from -127 to 127, and the result is held within that range. These are the same flags that code 47 sets and clears.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Each bribe adds 1 to flag 12. Use E1 = 12, E2 = 1, E3 = 1, E4 = 3, E5 = the guard-relents script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Compares a mission flag with a number and goes to one of two places.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Flag number.
2) Value to compare with.
3) Target type.
4) Target if the flag is less.
5) Target if the flag is equal or greater.
1) The flag is read as a signed number.
2) The flag counts as "equal or greater" when it is E2 or more.
3) 0 starts a script. 1 opens a simple encounter. 2 opens a typed encounter. Any other value does nothing.
4) The target number used when the flag is below E2.
5) The target number used otherwise.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A target of 0 means do not branch: the script goes on to the next action. To branch for only one outcome, leave the other target 0.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Flag 8 counts the king's goodwill. Use E1 = 8, E2 = 5, E3 = 0, E4 = the angry-king script, E5 = 0.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Goes to one place if every chosen warrior has a condition, and to another place if not.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Condition number.
2) Who is tested.
4) Script if all have it.
5) Script if not all do.
1) The condition number, as in code 43.

2) 0 tests the whole squad. -1 tests the picked warriors; if nobody is picked, the test passes. A positive number n tests only the warrior at place n counted from 0, so 1 is the second warrior; the first warrior can be tested only through 0 or -1.
4) The script to start when all tested warriors have the condition.
5) The script to start otherwise.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Any non-zero value counts as having the condition, including a permanent one. Dead warriors are included in the whole-squad test. Both targets must be real scripts. E3 is not read.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A healer sells her antidote only if the whole squad is poisoned. Use E1 = 3, E2 = 0, E4 = the sale script, E5 = the "not everyone needs it" script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: A registration check. In New Centurions it always passes.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The script goes on to the next action. You do not need to place this code.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: None needed.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Picks a random target number from a range and goes there.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Target type.
2) Lowest target.
3) Highest target.
4) Sound number.
5) Text number.
1) 0 starts a script. 1 opens a simple encounter. 2 opens a typed encounter. Any other value does nothing.
2) The lowest target number that can be chosen.
3) The highest target number that can be chosen, both ends included.
4) A sound played before the choice. 0 for none.
5) A text shown before the choice. 0 for none.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The sound and text come first, then one random number is drawn. Every target from E2 to E3 should exist.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: Three ambush scripts are numbered 20, 21 and 22. Use E1 = 0, E2 = 20, E3 = 22, E4 = a twig-snap sound, E5 = 0.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Tests one fact about the squad and goes to one of two places.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: A negative E2 limits tests 0, 1, 2, 5 and 6 to the picked warriors.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) The test.
2) The value tested.
3) Target type.
4) Target if true.
5) Target if false.

1) 0 asks whether a warrior of M.O.S. E2 is in the squad. 1 asks for race E2. 2 asks for gender E2. 3 asks whether the squad is aboard a boat. 4 asks whether the squad is camping. 5 asks for a warrior whose M.O.S. class is E2. 6 asks for a warrior whose race belongs to class E2. 7 asks whether the levels of all warriors added together are more than E2. 8 asks the same for the picked warriors only. Any other number counts as false.
2) The number tested. Tests 3 and 4 ignore it. The gender and class numbers are not listed in this manual; check them in your scenario before relying on them.
3) 0 starts a script. 1 opens a simple encounter. 2 opens a typed encounter.
4) The target number if the test is true.
5) The target number if it is false.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: A target of 0 means carry on with the next action. Use this to branch on only one outcome.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A ferryman refuses boats. Use E1 = 3, E3 = 0, E4 = the "no boats" script, E5 = 0.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Goes to one place if a certain ally is with the squad, and to another if not.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Monster number of the ally.
2) Target type.
3) If absent.
4) Target if present.
5) Target if absent.
1) The monster number, 0 to 127.
2) 0 starts a script. 1 opens a simple encounter. 2 opens a typed encounter.
3) 0 branches to E5 when the ally is absent. Any other value goes on to the next action.
4) The target number used when the ally is present, whatever E3 says.
5) The target number used when the ally is absent and E3 is 0.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The guide Tamsin is monster 33. Use E1 = 33, E2 = 0, E3 = 0, E4 = the "she leads the way" script, E5 = the "lost without a guide" script.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The monster number of the ally.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Takes an ally of that monster number out of the squad.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: When an ally in one of the first five places is removed, only the next ally's record is copied into its place, and the later allies stay where they were. With three allies A, B and C, removing A leaves B in two places and C gone from the list. If two allies of that monster number stand next to each other, the second one is copied over the first and is then itself replaced: X, X, C leaves just one X in the squad, and C is lost. Removing an ally from the sixth place or later only shortens the list, so the last ally drops out. If the squad has several allies, remove from the end of the list first, and test the result in your scenario.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: The wizard leaves after the tower falls. Use ID = his monster number.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: The monster number of the ally.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Adds a monster to the squad as an ally.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The ally is built from the monster's record. Its stamina is its bonus plus 1 to 8 for each hit die, and its maximum equals that stamina. For each difficulty level its psi resistance goes up by 3, each of its six saves by 7, its armor class down by 2 and its agility up by 1. An ally with a negative weapon entry is given a random weapon. A squad holds at most 20 allies; when full, a warning is shown and nobody is added.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A mercenary joins at the tavern. Use ID = the mercenary's monster number.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Moves victory points back off the squad. Each affected warrior's upgrade points go down by the amount, and the victory points he still has to earn go up by the same amount.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Amount of points.
2) Who is affected.
1) The amount can be any whole number. A negative amount does the reverse and gives points back.

2) 0 affects every warrior with the full amount. 2 divides the amount by the number of warriors in the squad (whole number division, so a remainder is lost) and gives each warrior that share. Any value other than 1 and 2 acts like 0. 1 is meant to mean "picked warriors only", but it does not work warrior by warrior: it looks at one party-pick entry, the one that matches this step's position in the script, and then treats the whole squad alike. Either every warrior changes or none does.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Nothing is taken from a single total. The two counters simply move in opposite directions by the same amount.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A cursed idol drains the squad. E1 = 500 and E2 = 2 in a squad of four takes 125 from each warrior's upgrade points.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Every warrior's pack is emptied onto the ground and the drop sound plays. The screen is refreshed afterward.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: Use this for scenes such as a flooded cell where the squad loses everything. Nothing here puts the items back anywhere you can reach; give the squad new gear with another code if the story needs it.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: A river crossing sweeps the squad's packs away. Run this code and follow it with a text that explains what happened.

sections.label: Caution
paragraphs: Test this in your scenario before relying on it for items that are cursed or locked in place.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: An Extra Codes number. The record that follows it (ID + 1) is also read.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: Changes the position, the size and the chance of one random-encounter rectangle of a land, so that the places where the squad is attacked can move as the story moves on.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs:
1) Land number.
2) Rectangle number.
3) Not used.
4) Amount added to the rectangle's encounter chance.
5) How the sides change.
1) The land to edit. It is saved when the change is done, and the land the squad stands in is loaded again.
2) A rectangle number from 0 to 19. The game does not check the number, so stay inside this range.
4) Added to the chance whatever E5 says. Use 0 to leave the chance alone.

5) -1 changes no sides. 0 sets the sides to the values in the second record. 1 slides the whole rectangle: E1 of the second record moves it across and E2 moves it down. 2 adds each of the four values to its own side.
The second record holds the four sides in this order: left, right, top, bottom. With mode 0 they are the new sides. With mode 2 they are added to the old ones, so negative numbers pull a side in.

sections.label: Note
paragraphs: The land is saved after the change, so the new rectangle stays for the rest of the game.

sections.label: Example
paragraphs: After the bandit camp is cleared, set E1 = 3, E2 = 4, E4 = -30 and E5 = -1 to make the wolves of land 3's rectangle 4 (the fifth one) much less likely.

sections.label: ID
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: Use
paragraphs: In the original game this stopped an unregistered copy: it showed a refusal and stepped the squad back. In this game registration is always satisfied, so the code does nothing and the script goes on to the next action.

sections.label: Options
paragraphs: None.

sections.label: E-Codes
paragraphs: None.
